failed_attempts: No failed PdM attempt built on third-party legal machine-data access found; the right applied only from 2025-09-12 so 'tried too early' cannot be shown. Industrial precedents (not PSD2): (1) Jahnke et al. (Wirtschaftsinformatik 2024) abstract: 'the success of data marketplaces in the industrial sector has been poor' (reason offered: centralised architectures limit data-provider sovereignty; no adoption figures in abstract). (2) Manufacturing-X: Bitkom survey (reported 2024-04-18) found 1% of industrial firms involved and 4% planning to join. (3) Automotive: independent aftermarket still lacked interoperable in-vehicle data access in Oct 2021 under the OEM 'extended vehicle' model (Professional Motor Mechanic 2021-10-29); a sector law was only expected. (4) senseering / MachineDataMarketplace.NRW: senseering is listed active by CB Insights (founded 2018, Cologne) but the marketplace outcome was not found. (5) Catena-X has no PdM app (absence.csv, Cofinity-X June 2026).
blockers: Scope: Art. 2(15) 'product data' = data 'the manufacturer designed to be retrievable' (OEM controls what is exposed); Commission FAQ (via DLA Piper 2024-09-23) puts data 'inferred or derived ... through the use of algorithms or other additional investments' out of scope, so PdM outputs are excluded while raw and pre-processed signals are in; Nortal 2025-11-17 and mybusinessfuture 2026-09-29 repeat this. Trade secrets: Art. 4(6) secrets preserved and disclosed only with protective measures; Art. 4(7) holder may withhold or suspend; Art. 4(8) case-by-case refusal if serious economic damage is highly likely; Art. 5(9) to 5(11) mirror this for third parties, with Art. 37 authority notification. Art. 5(3): gatekeepers cannot be recipients. Art. 4(1) and 5(1): free of charge to the user, but Art. 5(1) routes to Arts. 8 and 9, so the recipient can be charged reasonable (FRAND) compensation that 'may include a margin'; Art. 9(4) caps SME recipients at the cost of making data available (Commission draft guidelines of 2026-02-02 confirm no margin for SMEs). Competing-product limit applies to developing a connected product (Art. 4(10) per springlex); Commission FAQ says it does not reach related services such as maintenance. Enforcement: per Simmons & Simmons (2026-09-02) only Denmark, Finland, Germany, Lithuania, Malta and the Netherlands have implemented, France partially, 20 states pending; Germany's DADG in force 2026-05-30 with BNetzA as authority (top fine tier EUR 5M per DLA Piper 2026-03-31). Market: the installed base is mostly pre-2026 equipment and the Art. 3(1) design-for-access duty applies only to products placed after 2026-09-12 (retrofit portals do not satisfy it per mybusinessfuture). GEA notice shows OEM practice: raw MQTT data yes, processed data and competing maintenance providers restricted. Demand side: Manufacturing-X participation 1% (2024).
blocker_trend: Mixed. Falling: Art. 3(1) design duty live since 2026-09-12; unfair-terms rules reach older long-term contracts from 2027-09-12 (Art. 50 as mirrored by springlex); national enforcement spreading (Germany 2026-05-30); SME cost cap on compensation. Rising: Digital Omnibus (COM(2025)837) would drop the 'exceptional circumstances' qualifier, lower 'highly likely' to 'likely' and add a third-country-risk refusal ground (NatLawReview 2026-07-15); Council mandate sought in Coreper note 10729/26 dated 2026-06-22 (trade-secret recital 11); Parliament (ITRE and LIBE) position outstanding; still a proposal as of 2026-09-29. Net: scope and trade-secret blockers rising or flat, access mechanics falling.
note: Label UNTRIED, with low confidence that it stays so: nothing found has been tried and failed, and the lever is 13 months old. If forced to a second choice it would be BLOCKED (scope, trade-secret refusal, thin installed-base coverage). No PdM provider found saying it uses or will use Data Act rights: searches this round (Tractian, Augury, Nanoprecise, I-care, Senseye, wind operators) returned only explainers and OEM-side compliance.
